title: Pertamina Eco RunFest 2026 Review: Jakarta's World Athletics Label Half Marathon
seo_title: Pertamina Eco RunFest 2026 Review | Jakarta Half Marathon
meta_description: Pertamina Eco RunFest 2026 review: the World Athletics Label half marathon in central Jakarta, its seven eco initiatives, four distances, and a date that moved.
dek: A 13th-edition, World Athletics Label road race through central Jakarta, built as much around waste reduction as around running. Four distances, a 14,000-runner target, and a published date that two sets of sources disagree about.
verdict: Pertamina Eco RunFest is one of the few Southeast Asian road races carrying a World Athletics Label [1], which puts it in a different administrative bracket from most of the region's city runs: measured course, recognised results, and a field that has previously drawn runners from more than 20 countries [3]. The 2026 edition is the 13th, themed 'Spark the Change, Leave Zero Trace', and targets 14,000 runners and 10,000 visitors around Gelora Bung Karno and Istora Senayan [2]. The environmental framing is not decoration -- the organisers say 100 percent of ticket sale profits go to their eco programme [2]. The one thing to confirm before booking is the date, which sources do not agree on; see below.

sections.heading: A World Athletics Label Race in Central Jakarta
paragraphs: The event is listed as a World Athletics Label road race in Jakarta [1], which is the detail that separates it from the bulk of the region's corporate-sponsored city runs. A Label means the course, the timing and the results administration meet a published international standard, and it is the reason the race can credibly market itself to overseas runners rather than only to the domestic field.

The 2026 edition is the 13th, and the organisers are targeting 14,000 runners plus 10,000 spectators, based around the Gelora Bung Karno complex and Istora Senayan in central Jakarta [2]. That is a large field by regional standards, and a venue that comes with its own transport links rather than requiring a shuttle from the middle of nowhere.

Previous editions have drawn participants from more than 20 countries, though the organisers have said they are increasing the allocation for domestic runners this year [3]. If you are entering from abroad, that is worth reading as a reason not to leave registration late.

sections.heading: Seven Eco Initiatives, and Where the Ticket Money Goes
paragraphs: The 'Eco' in the name is carried by seven sustainability programmes rather than a slogan. They include Eco Innovation, a roadshow taking waste-management education into schools; a race jersey made from recycled waste material in collaboration with Manta Liberta; an Eco Talent strand using influencers and public figures to push environmental messaging; and waste management operated across the event itself, with a stated focus on cutting plastic [3].

The financial commitment behind it is unusually specific. Pertamina's VP of corporate communication has stated that 100 percent of the profit from ticket sales goes to the eco programme [2]. Most races that market themselves as green are describing their own operations; this one is describing where the money ends up, which is a claim a reader can hold the organiser to.

Whether any of that changes your race is a separate question. It does not make the course faster or the weather kinder. But if you are choosing between comparable Jakarta events, it is a real differentiator rather than a marketing one.

sections.heading: Four Distances, From a 1.5K to the Half
paragraphs: The event runs four distances: 1.5 km, 5 km, 10 km and the 21.0975 km half marathon [1]. That spread is deliberate for a race that describes itself as a festival as much as a competition -- the 1.5 km exists so that families and first-timers have somewhere to start, while the half is the distance carrying the World Athletics Label billing.

The route is described as running through the heart of the capital [1]. Central Jakarta on a closed-road Sunday morning is a genuinely good place to run: flat, wide, and briefly free of the traffic that otherwise defines the city. Expect heat and humidity regardless of the start time -- Jakarta sits barely six degrees south of the equator, and December is inside the wet season.

sections.heading: A Date Worth Confirming Before You Book
paragraphs: Sources do not agree on when the 2026 edition is held, and this is the single most important thing to check before committing to flights. Two Indonesian reports published in late August and September 2026 both give the date as 6 December 2026, with consistent supporting detail -- the Gelora Bung Karno and Istora Senayan venue, the 13th edition, the 'Spark the Change, Leave Zero Trace' theme and the 14,000-runner target [2][3].

The international race aggregator listing for the same event instead shows 22 November 2026 [1]. That is the earlier of the two, and aggregator listings are frequently the last thing an organiser updates when a date moves.

On the balance of evidence this listing follows the December date, because two independently published contemporaneous local reports carrying matching venue, edition and theme detail are stronger evidence than a single aggregator row. It is not certain. Check the official registration channel before booking anything non-refundable.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: For a half marathon in Jakarta, this is the strongest option on paper: a World Athletics Label [1], a central-city course [1], an organiser large enough to close roads properly, and a field in the tens of thousands [2]. The environmental programme is more substantial than the category usually gets, and the ticket-revenue commitment is specific enough to be checkable [2].

The reservations are the ordinary ones for an equatorial city race -- heat, humidity, and a large field on closed roads meaning congestion in the opening kilometres -- plus the unresolved date. Entry fees have not been published in the sources reviewed here, so treat cost as unknown.
This listing was compiled from published reporting and the organisers' own announcements before the event took place. It is not a first-hand race report.

faqs.question: When is Pertamina Eco RunFest 2026?
faqs.answer: Sources disagree. Two Indonesian reports from late 2026 give 6 December 2026, with matching venue, edition and theme detail; an international aggregator listing shows 22 November 2026. This listing follows the December date, but confirm with the official registration channel before booking travel.

faqs.question: What distances does Pertamina Eco RunFest offer?
faqs.answer: Four: 1.5 km, 5 km, 10 km and the 21.0975 km half marathon. The 1.5 km is aimed at families and first-time participants, while the half marathon is the distance behind the event's World Athletics Label billing.

faqs.question: What makes Pertamina Eco RunFest an eco event?
faqs.answer: Seven sustainability programmes, including waste-management education roadshows in schools, a race jersey made from recycled waste material, an environmental messaging strand, and waste management across the event. The organisers state that 100 percent of ticket sale profits fund the eco programme.

faqs.question: Where does Pertamina Eco RunFest start?
faqs.answer: The 2026 edition is based around the Gelora Bung Karno complex and Istora Senayan in central Jakarta, with a route described as running through the heart of the capital. The organisers are targeting 14,000 runners and 10,000 visitors.

editorial_notes: Compiled 2026-09-09. No rating is given: the race has not been run. The event date is disputed between sources and is discussed openly in the body rather than resolved silently; the entity record was updated to 2026-12-06 on the same evidence and flagged needs_review.
